article_title: Guided group reflection versus SNAPPS in enhancing clinical reasoning in final-year MBBS students at a public-sector teaching hospital in Pakistan: a quasi-experimental study.
citation: Anjum Nida; Yasmin Rahila; Khurram Muhammad; Shan Saima; Ali Shabana. (2026). Guided group reflection versus SNAPPS in enhancing clinical reasoning in final-year MBBS students at a public-sector teaching hospital in Pakistan: a quasi-experimental study. BMJ Open. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2025-115534
title: Guided group reflection using the Mamede and Schmidt deliberate reflection framework
description: GGR is a six-step structured group reflection intervention delivered in 60-minute case-based sessions, following "the deliberate reflection framework described by Mamede and Schmidt". Steps move from initial hypothesis generation through identifying supportive, contradictory and missing findings, generating alternative hypotheses, to prioritising differentials with facilitator feedback. The article uses it as the collaborative comparator to SNAPPS in undergraduate clinical teaching.
requirements: Trained facilitators; each 60-min session facilitated by trained instructors with a 60-min orientation
constraints: Sessions were conducted in separate medical units to minimise contamination
examples: Four weekly case sessions covering chronic dyspnoea, anaemia, chronic liver disease and chronic diarrhoea
key_sources: Anjum Nida; Yasmin Rahila; Khurram Muhammad; Shan Saima; Ali Shabana. (2026). Guided group reflection versus SNAPPS in enhancing clinical reasoning in final-year MBBS students at a public-sector teaching hospital in Pakistan: a quasi-experimental study. article_title: Genomic competence among nurses: A spotlight on ethics.
citation: Laaksonen M, Paavilainen E, Koivisto A-M, Halkoaho A. (2025). Genomic competence among nurses: A spotlight on ethics. Nursing Ethics, 32(8). https://doi.org/10.1177/09697330251366594
title: GGNPS-CA: ethics-enhanced Canadian Adaptation of the Genetics and Genomics Nursing Practice Survey
description: The GGNPS-CA is a modified version of the Genetics and Genomics Nursing Practice Survey that "retains the original framework while incorporating an important new dimension: ethics". It covers attitudes, receptivity, confidence, genomic knowledge, social system, and adoption domains grounded in Rogers' Diffusion of Innovation theory, adding three direct and four indirect ethical questions and a 12-item Knowledge Score. This study translated it into Finnish, replaced one knowledge question, and administered it via REDCap; the Finnish version was back-translated and approved with the developers.
requirements: Respondents must be Finnish-speaking registered nurses; the instrument was translated, back-translated and collectively approved with the GGNPS-CA developers for the Finnish context
constraints: The GGNPS-CA has not yet been validated, although the original GGNPS has; the Finnish version changed one Knowledge Score question and omitted one ethics question, limiting direct comparison with prior surveys
target_learners: Registered nurses, public health nurses, midwives and paramedics with a registered nursing degree
target_learning_goals: Assessing genomic knowledge, competence, confidence and ethical awareness of nursing professionals
examples: Administered online between October 30 and December 31, 2023, reaching 234 Finnish registered nurses via three professional associations
key_sources: Laaksonen M, Paavilainen E, Koivisto A-M, Halkoaho A. (2025). Genomic competence among nurses: A spotlight on ethics. Nursing Ethics, 32(8). https://doi.org/10.1177/09697330251366594
